summary: The instruction, manual HC-4, README and shipped package together determine every graded figure. The two figures the manual leaves open (shift dose of a survey below three quarters of its shift, and the level a reading above 115.0 dBA is counted at) are disclosed as 'keep today's step, worked from the manual-defined figures'. The shipped code fixes both, and every sealed expectation and differential pair I traced agrees with that reading. I found no hidden tie-break, rounding, boundary or format rule.
checks_performed: Reconciled the 57 files listed in packet-manifest.json against the Glob listing and read each one. tests/expected/limits_workers.jsonl was truncated by Read at 40,593 characters; the rest (report rows L160-L299 and all 40 group rows) was read with Grep -o. tests/expected/limits_logs.jsonl was read in full as consecutive 290-character Grep -o chunks.
Mapped each manual rule (1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 2.2-2.6, 3.1-3.3, 4.1, 5.1-5.3, 6.1) and each README report key to the test that grades it in tests/test_outputs.py.

Identified the figures the manual leaves open: the shift dose of a survey below three quarters of its shift (3.3 covers only partial and whole-or-longer surveys) and the counted level of a reading above 115.0 dBA (2.3 fixes only readings at or below the ceiling). Confirmed that instruction.md:3 sends both back to today's step, and that shipped shift.py:17-22 and runs.py:19 fix those steps.

Hand-traced the sealed expectations against manual plus instruction. Checked: HC4-0015 X1/X2/X3, HC4-0016 Y1-Y6, HC4-0037 V1/V2 (sub-3/4 surveys, with manual sampled time including quiet readings); HC4-0019 Y1, HC4-0020 Z1/Z2, HC4-0038 K1/K4 and the G1/G2 group rows (above-ceiling readings counted at 115.0); HC4-0005 and HC4-0006 (sampled time); HC4-0009/0010 (partial projection); HC4-0011/0012 (whole shift); HC4-0013/0014 (exactly three quarters, including 458 of 610); HC4-0017/0018 (measured nothing); HC4-0024/0025 (rounding and status bands); HC4-0022/0039 (impulse at 140.0); HC4-0023 (TWA formula and null); HC4-0027/0028 (quiet members); HC4-0029 (group code order); L-2880 and L-PEAKS in HC4-0031; L280 in HC4-0030; and the generated rows GD6H5, K1-W9-A, 7NE64-ZB, YF5SBEZ6DM93 and XVOZG. Every traced value matches the contract.

Checked the differential pairs: every below-three-quarters pair differs only in shift_minutes, with both surveys below three quarters. Today's step (shift.py:17-22) does not read the shift, so equal doses follow from the disclosed rule. Above-ceiling pairs differ only in a reading above 115.0 against the same reading at 115.0, which is equal under today's min(level, CEILING_DBA). Measured-nothing pairs have sampled time 0, which gives today's 0.0.

Checked test_section_one_largest_doses cases X4, X3 and X6 against manual 3.3/4.1: 1,920 minutes on a 480-minute shift keeps its measured dose, 1,080 of 1,440 minutes is exactly three quarters and projects, and 2,880 minutes on a 60-minute shift keeps its measured dose.

Checked the dose tolerance statement (instruction.md:5) against _number (test_outputs.py:196-199, REL=ABS=5e-11) and the 12-significant-figure sealed doses. Also checked that exact TWA halves cannot occur in this domain: every dose lies in Q(2^(1/30)), and a TWA ending in .x5 needs 2^(odd/60). So the 'exact half going up' rule never conflicts with the graded tenths.

Checked the report schema: README.md:29-41 against _row/compare (test_outputs.py:202-225). This covers key sets, the booleans, null TWA, extra keys, and the group-row ceiling/impulse rejection against manual 6.1.

Checked the relabelling (test_outputs.py:350-380) against the contract: survey name 'as given' as any string, new ids within 1.4, workers shuffled and report order following, runs split at their own level. The split leaves sampled time, measured dose, flags and group codes unchanged.

coverage_sweep.category: Every grading rule traced to a sentence or authoritative candidate-visible artifact
coverage_sweep.reason: Each test in test_outputs.py maps to a manual rule or README key. The two open figures are covered by instruction.md:3 ('keep the figure that step works out today, from the figures the manual does define'), and the shipped package that the candidate edits fixes them.

coverage_sweep.category: Input domain and needed boundaries specified
coverage_sweep.reason: Manual 1.4 sets the domain and instruction.md:3 lists the out-of-domain inputs that are left open. The graded boundaries are the 80.0 threshold (inclusive), the 40.0 reading floor, 0.0 non-readings, exactly three quarters of the shift (inclusive), the whole shift, 115.0 (not flagged), 140.0 dBC (an impulse), the 82.0/85.0 bands on the reported TWA, and dose 0 giving no TWA. The manual states each one. within_limits (test_outputs.py:154-166) keeps graded surveys inside 1.4.

coverage_sweep.category: Rendered instruction, declared artifacts and verifier paths agree
coverage_sweep.reason: The instruction command 'python3 /app/tools/noisedose_run.py SURVEY.json' matches reduce() (test_outputs.py:130-147). The byte-identical driver requirement matches _install_driver and test_submitted_driver_unchanged. artifacts=['/app/'] covers /app/src. There is no broken template text or test sentinel.

examples/press-shop-day.json uses only in-domain inputs: 0.0 runs, quiet readings, 480/600-minute shifts and a 142.6 dBC peak. Its narrative matches the symptoms named in instruction.md:1. No expected output is shipped, so there is nothing to contradict.

Group order is stated in the README ('ascending character order ... digits before letters'). Rounding is to the nearest tenth, half up (1.2). Exact halves are unreachable, so round-half-even and half-up agree on every graded TWA. Worker order is survey order. Group mean is sum/count (1.3). No undisclosed tie-break exists.

instruction.md:5 discloses that twa is compared exactly (same tenth or null) and that dose has a stated tolerance. The verifier accepts int or float numbers, accepts extra keys on worker rows and at top level, and parses JSON rather than comparing text. Rejecting ceiling/impulse keys on group rows is backed by manual 6.1 ('a group carries no ceiling or impulse flag') and by the four-key group row in the README.

Every instruction promise (limits, 1,500-run and 2,880-minute logs, 140.0 dBC peaks, exact-boundary TWAs, quiet workers, one- and many-member groups) has a family. Every test expectation traces to the manual or to the disclosed keep-today rule. Manual, README and instruction do not contradict each other.

Everything is computable with the standard library in /app/src. The driver is unchanged and adds /app/src to sys.path, so running under -I -S does not break a stdlib-only package. The dose tolerance (5e-11 relative) is well above float summation error for up to 1,500 runs.
